prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on my research, here are the official rate limits for the GitHub REST API.

The rate limits differ significantly between unauthenticated and authenticated requests.

For unauthenticated requests, the limit is much lower and is based on the originating IP address.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limiting
**QUOTE:** "For unauthenticated requests, the rate limit allows for up to 60 requests per hour."
**CLAIM:** The rate limit for unauthenticated requests to the GitHub REST API is 60 requests per hour.

For authenticated requests, the limit is much higher and is tied to your user account or OAuth application.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limiting
**QUOTE:** "For API requests using Basic Authentication or OAuth, you can make up to 5,000 requests per hour."
**CLAIM:** The standard rate limit for authenticated requests to the GitHub REST API is 5,000 requests per hour.

The documentation also notes that some requests to the Search API have a separate, more restrictive limit, regardless of authentication.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/search?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limit
**QUOTE:** "The Search API has a custom rate limit. For requests using Basic Authentication, OAuth, or a personal access token, you can make up to 30 requests per minute."
**CLAIM:** The rate limit for the Search API is 30 requests per minute for authenticated requests.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/search?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limit
**QUOTE:** "For unauthenticated requests, the rate limit allows you to make up to 10 requests per minute."
**CLAIM:** The rate limit for the Search API is 10 requests per minute for unauthenticated requests.

Finally, the response headers from the API provide information about your current rate limit status.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limiting
**QUOTE:** "The rate limit status is returned in the headers of all API requests."
**CLAIM:** The `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, and `x-ratelimit-reset` headers provide the current rate limit status.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limit-http-headers
**QUOTE:** "`x-ratelimit-limit`: The maximum number of requests you're permitted to make per hour."
**CLAIM:** The `x-ratelimit-limit` header shows your maximum permitted requests per hour.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limit-http-headers
**QUOTE:** "`x-ratelimit-remaining`: The number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window."
**CLAIM:** The `x-ratelimit-remaining` header shows how many requests you have left for the current window.

**SOURCE:** https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28#rate-limit-http-headers
**QUOTE:** "`x-ratelimit-reset`: The time at which the current rate limit window resets in UTC epoch seconds."
**CLAIM:** The `x-ratelimit-reset` header shows when the current rate limit window will reset.
